response.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_of_avg_length, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM per_rating;

assumptions.assumption: The ratio is computed per film as rental_rate / replacement_cost, then averaged within each rating. The CAST to DOUBLE avoids MySQL's fixed-scale decimal division so the result stays unrounded.

AVG(length) skips NULL lengths, which is how 'ignoring missing values' is applied to running time. rental_rate is NOT NULL and replacement_cost > 20.99 excludes zero, so the ratio has no missing or divide-by-zero cases.
No film has a NULL rating. The verified per-rating counts (178 + 210 + 194 + 223 + 195 = 1000) cover every film, so no NULL group exists.

alternatives.interpretation: The 'average ratio' is read as a ratio of averages: average rental_rate divided by average replacement_cost within each rating, rather than the mean of per-film ratios.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(replacement_cost) AS ratio_of_avgs FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_of_avg_length, AVG(ratio_of_avgs) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM per_rating;
